description: Hand-labelled ground truth for the OWASP crAPI external target. Each probe is driven through the real BolaValidator by bench-crapi (owner / attacker / anonymous exchanges against a live compose stack). A probe matches a runner observation on (endpoint, attacker_profile, object_id). expected_label is what the validator MUST conclude. Authored from crAPI's own documented challenge list (docs/challenges.md) plus two realistic decoys.

vulnerabilities.rationale: crAPI Challenge 1 (docs/challenges.md). VehicleController.getLocationBOLA (services/identity/.../VehicleController.java) returns a vehicle's location by GUID with NO ownership check. A different authenticated user (Pogba) reads owner Adam's vehicle location + email. Confirmed live: attacker HTTP 200 with Adam's 32.778889/-91.919243/adam007@example.com; anonymous HTTP 401.

decoys.rationale: ProfileServiceImpl.getProfileVideo resolves the video from the CALLER's own user id and only returns it when the id matches, so a non-owner gets HTTP 404 'Video not found'. This endpoint looks cross-user-reachable (a numeric video id in the path) but ownership IS enforced. Confirmed live: owner Adam HTTP 200 (Adam_video), attacker Pogba HTTP 404. A naive cross-id scanner would flag the path; the validator correctly Rejects (attacker blocked).

The JWKS endpoint is intentionally public infrastructure data (clients need it to verify tokens) — the anonymous caller also receives the identical body. The validator observes anonymous success with a near-identical body and Rejects (public data is not a cross-user BOLA — the DVGA public-paste pattern). Confirmed live: anonymous HTTP 200 with the RSA key set.
